full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: These two rule by the defendant No. 1 petitioner directed against order dated 16-9-2010 passed by the learned District Judge, Nilphamari in Judicial Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 2010 and Judicial Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2010 rejecting the application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure thereby refusing to transfer Other Class Suit No. 4 of 2006 and other class suit No. 26 of 2003 from the Court of Mr Md Abdur Rashid Mia, learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Nilphamari to any other Court competent to try the same. 

 4. Learned Judge rejected the same finding that these grounds for transfer of the case are wild allegations, not supported by any evidence. 

 6. Mr. Md. Iqbal Hossain, learned Advocate, for the opposite party, on the other hand, submits that, he has no objection if the cases be tried by a different Court but he prays for early disposal of the suit as the suits are very old. Learned Advocate further submits that the plea for transfer of the suits taken by the petitioner is nothing but to delay in disposal of the suits, as such, order may be passed so that the suits may be disposed of expeditiously. 

 7. Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure give jurisdiction to learned District Judge to transfer a case/suit from one Court to another within his territorial Jurisdiction. Section 24 of the Code runs as follows:— 

 8. In the case of Pushpa Devi Saraf and another vs Jai Narain Parasrampuria AIR 1992 (SC) 1133, it has been held that when a petition for transfer of suit is filed making allegations against the Presiding Officer, the report if and when called for from him, should normally be confined to the allegations made against the impartiality or fairness of the judge and not with respect to the correctness or otherwise of the orders passed by him. 

 9. The case of Haji Md. Elias vs Mrs. Suraya Rahme, 1981 BLD 147, where it has been held on the submissions of Mr. MH Khandker who drew attention of the Court to the case of Md. Shamsul Huda vs Md. Mozammel Huq in which case their Lordship considered the relevant facts and observed in the following terms:— 

 "It is not a question of actual existence of a bias in a judge, but is a question as to whether the litigant may have reasonable apprehension about a fair trial. The test is whether a man of ordinary prudence may have an apprehension about a judicial officer's ability to maintain a standard of even-handed justice in regard to a particular case, because it is not only that justice is to be done, but also that justice should appear to be done. The apprehension, in our opinion, must have some objectivity. It is not merely an illusions or a stage of mental attitude. We are satisfied from the materials on record that the apprehension entertained by the defendant is not altogether without foundation." 

 10. The case of Vijaykumar vs Smt. Lima Sangh, AIR 1987 MP 41, a single Bench of Indore Bench held that, the crucial question, which falls for considerations is whether there was any ground made out for transfer of appeals pending before the Addl. District Judge and whether not granting interim stay of operation of the order appealed against would itself justify transfer of a pending appeal from one Court to another. The question is about transfer and that too on the ground indicated above. In section 24, CPC, following grounds have been held to be good grounds for involving section 24, CPC (a) reasonable apprehension of the litigant that he might not get justice in the Court in which the suit is pending; (b) the Judge having an interest in the lis, (c) importance and the difficulty of the question involved in the case, and (d) lastly, where the interests of justice require a transfer. As against the dismissal of stay application, the remedy does not lie in a transfer petition and in the background of facts, what was stated before the District Judge is not to be born out from the record. The order sheets date 3-4-1986 and 1-5-1986 do not even remotely suggest that there was any such dialogue between the respondents' counsel and the Judge, which warranted an inference that the judge was out to thwart urgency under the clock of vacation. 

 11. In the case of Alen vs Narayan, AIR 1949 Mad 283, it has been held that, 'District Judge derives unfettered power of transfer or withdrawal of a case under section 24. In that case it has further been held that Additional District Judge shall be deemed to be subordinate to the District Judge'. 

 12. In the case of Mohammad vs Abul, 42 DLR 21, and Bejoy vs Narendra 43 DLR 68 it has been held that, 'District Judge enjoy the power under this section somewhat of administrative nature and discretionary. In suitable case the District Judge can even suo moto exercise this power in the interest of justice. In the case of Bijoy vs Narendra. 43 DLR 68, it has further been held that District Judge can transfer a case when it is heard-in-part. 

 13. In the case of Tambia vs Abdur, 46 DLR 521 and Sadrul vs Asaduzzaman, 4 BLC 340, it has been held that in transferring a case from one Court to another the convenience of transfer which is to be taken into consideration by the Court is the convenience of both the parties. In the case of Nurul vs Janata Bank, 58 DLR 589 it has been held that the burden of establishing sufficient grounds for transfer lies heavily upon the application. In the case of Shamsul vs Mozammel, 27 DLR 43 it has been held that balance of convenience or expense in the matter of examination of witnesses of the parties has been recognized as a good ground for a transfer and it has further held that convenience of both the parties is to be taken into consideration. 

 14. In the case of Anwar vs Mand. 47 DLR 530 it has been held that utterance of any party outside the Court cannot be a sufficient ground for transferring a suit. In the case of Elias vs Suraiya 1981 BLD 147 it has been held apprehension of not getting fair trial is a ground for transfer but apprehension must have some objectivity. 

 15. The case of Kashem vs Md, 10 BLC 392 discard the ground that petitioner saw the opposite parties entering into the chamber of the judge as being hypersensitive or trivial or mini grievance. In the case of Standard Bank vs Farook, 10 BLC 414, it has been held that suspicion unless supported by particular and solid materials cannot be ground for a transfer of a case. 

 16. In the case of Zahir vs Yakuab, 43 DLR 168 it is held that transferee Court need not have territorial jurisdiction over the subject matter of the suit transferred. 

 17. It is established that the principal of transfer based on the doctrine of forum non-convenience and for preventing any failure of justice. The initial conditions for transfer the case that it should be filed at the earliest possible time and next, before settlement of issues. 

 18. The allegations made in the application for transfer to our mind are too wild and also that these are not valid grounds for transferring the case. Moreover, we find that in support of the statement made in the application no affidavit has been sworned by the petitioner but verification has been made which is not legal. The allegations mentioned in the application to our consideration are not come within the purview of section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 19. But on the last submission made by the learned Advocate on reference to annexure C and also to the order dated 11-8-2010 i.e. Order No. 8 we find that learned Judge after passing the impugned order of which the certified copy has been annexed (Annexure C) in the rule petition interpolated or add further line after (dari) as এবং যুক্তিতর্ক শুনানী’ which has been made so cleverly, so minutely and so masterly that it is very difficult to notice or find the addition. We find 'a' of 'Ant' has been mischievously added with the (dari) which only not been heinous, contemptuous but a misconduct on the part of the presiding judge and specifically open his mind that he is interested in disposing of this matter even at the expense of the defendant which cannot be allowed. A Judge always be impartial and act with his conscious for which he is answerable to "Allah" and "Allah" alone, not to anybody. 

 20. We are not making any aspersion on the conduct of the learned Judge but we cautious him that in future such type of misconduct if found then we shall taken proper action against him.
